unite_adi: REGULAR UPPER SECONDARY-YEAR 11-LEVEL: B1.3 THEME 3: PERSONAL LIFE & WELL-BEING

bolumler.ogrenmeKanitlari: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students will explore the theme of ''Personal Life and Well-Being'' by focusing on how both physical and mental/emotional health contribute to overall well-being. Students are asked to research and present a comprehensive project that addresses two key aspects: maintaining physical health and nurturing mental and emotional health. They will analyse the importance of balancing both aspects to ensure a healthy lifestyle and discuss the ways in which physical and mental health are interconnected. Students will create a multimedia presentation (such as a video, slideshow) that highlights personal strategies for improving well-being, reflects on how their own habits affect their health, and includes advice or tips on maintaining physical and emotional balance. The final presentation should also include a reflection on how social pressures, technology, and modern life impact well-being, offering a critical look at how to navigate these challenges for better health. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme. Öğrenme-Öğretme Yaşantıları
bolumler.temelKabuller: This theme includes the concept of ''personal life and well-being with its components such as providing well- being with physical health (body and illnesses); providing well-being with mental and emotional health'' and it is assumed that it could be present in almost all languages, with some exceptions. It is assumed that a student of an upper secondary school in year 11 may know what personal life and well-being, providing well- being with physical health (body and illnesses); providing well-being with mental and emotional health mean in their own language as it is known that almost all people who start to learn a new language bring their pre- existing knowledge (in their own language) with them and transfer it to their new language learning context. However, they may not know how to say these things in another language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. Fortunately, this existing knowledge in their own language can help them recognise, understand, and learn them more easily in a foreign language, in this case English. As they are students of an upper secondary school in year 11, they are expected to know some basic vocabulary about ''personal life and well-being'' in English from previous themes and/or years such as ''a hand, cold, flu, headache, to wear'' and also some structures such as ''What’s the matter with you? Do you have the flu? How does she feel? Is it boring to live without a smartphone?'' in English from the previous themes and/ or years. These grammar items and vocabulary are revised during the ''Revision Programme'' at the beginning of the year and they can be used as a basis for learning the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme, so that the new grammatical elements in the current theme can be learnt easily.
bolumler.onDegerlendirme: It is assumed that these students in an upper secondary school are ready to learn the concept of ''personal life and well-being with its components such as providing well-being with physical health (body and illnesses); providing well-being with mental and emotional health'' cognitively, affectively, and socially since it is appropriate to their age and language level. Therefore, a contextual poster or a large picture could be provided for the students to remember and practise the items that they are related and previously learnt so that they can discuss the poster and/or the picture in pairs and write down what they remember. This session can help them revise all the related vocabulary and grammatical elements that they have already learnt from previous themes or from previous years as a preparatory practice. In this way, their performance can be evaluated in terms of how much they remember and how accurately they use these items to build their competence in the current theme. It can help the teacher decide what to emphasise, revise, and practise in order to facilitate the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme. (Their performance can be evaluated by rubrics, a rating scale, and /or a marking scheme during these practices.).
bolumler.zenginlestirme: Objective: To create and share future plans for physical and mental well-being in English, through their speaking and writing skills by using target vocabulary. Activity 1: Future Well-being Plan Students create a future plan for their well-being, focusing on physical and mental health and sustainability. They use target vocabulary such as ''balanced diet'', ''adequate sleep'', ''to manage'', ''to exercise'', and ''to set goals''. For example, a student might write, ''In the future, I will eat a balanced diet and do yoga to stay strong, and I will practice mindfulness to feel calm''. After writing their plans, students share them in small groups and compare their ideas using sentences like, ''My plan is more relaxing than my current habits'', or ''It will be as healthy as my diet now but more fun''. The teacher gives feedback on vocabulary use, grammar, and pronunciation. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
bolumler.destekleme: Objective: To discuss problems and provide supportive advice in a context in English through a role play activity by using the target vocabulary. Activity 1: Friendly Advice Chat Students work in pairs as two friends having a conversation about their problems. The teacher prepares papers with symptoms and related advice (e.g., ''low energy—get adequate sleep'') and places them in a box. Each pair selects a paper, and Friend A shares their problem using target vocabulary (e.g., ''I feel frustrated because I have low energy''.), while Friend B listens and offers supportive advice based on the paper (e.g., ''You should get adequate sleep and try mindfulness exercises''). After each pair performs, the teacher provides constructive feedback focusing on pronunciation, sentence accuracy. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
